'''Horace Jenkins''' (born October 14, 1974) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and several teams in Europe and Israel.

==High school==
Jenkins graduated from [[New Jersey]]'s [[Elizabeth High School (New Jersey)|Elizabeth High School]] in 1993.

==College career==
Jenkins played one season at [[Union County College]], before leaving to tend to the birth of his son, Hakeem.<ref>Coffey, Wayne. [http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/sports/2001/04/22/2001-04-22_make_room_for_daddy__horace_.html "MAKE ROOM FOR DADDY Horace Jenkins, 26, goes from William Paterson to possible NBA first-round pick"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090306202145/http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/sports/2001/04/22/2001-04-22_make_room_for_daddy__horace_.html |date=2009-03-06 }}, ''[[New York Daily News]]'', April 22, 2001. Accessed March 1, 2008. "It is a prodigious jump, even for someone with a 44-inch vertical leap. It is even more impressive, considering that Jenkins: Never played his senior year at Elizabeth High School"</ref> Over the next three and a half years, Jenkins worked for the [[United States Postal Service]], as an electrician, and on the back of a garbage truck. Once he saved up some money, he decided he wanted to go back to college, and play basketball.<ref name=nytimes>[https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9B07E4DE1731F931A35754C0A9649C8B63&sec=&spon=&pagewanted=print PRO BASKETBALL; N.B.A. Dream Is Alive For Jenkins, Almost 28 – New York Times<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

While at [[William Paterson University]], Jenkins was a three-time [[Division III (NCAA)|Division III]] Player of the Year (1999, 2000, and 2001). He was also a three-time Division III All-American. He holds numerous school records, and also was named 2001 Basketball Times Division III Player of the Year. Jenkins was also the winner of the 2001 ESPN NCAA dunk contest, beating former [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] standout [[Jeff Trepagnier]]. [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]'s Trepagnier, one of college's most prolific high flyers, missed his last dunk attempt, and the {{convert|6|ft|1|in|m|adj=on}} Jenkins, had one up his sleeve, wrapping it up with a foul line two-foot leaner.

==Professional career==
Jenkins attended all three [[NBA]] pre-draft camps, but he was undrafted in the [[2001 NBA draft]]. In the summer of 2001, Jenkins attended rookie camp with the [[Orlando Magic]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.d3hoops.com/notable/01/june01.htm |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2007-10-07 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705155201/http://www.d3hoops.com/notable/01/june01.htm |archivedate=2008-07-05 }}</ref> and also received an invitation to training camp with Orlando. However, he declined the invitation, and signed with [[Cimberio Borgomanero]], a team in the [[Serie A2 Basket|Italian second league]]. He received a guaranteed one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.d3hoops.com/notable/01/julyaugsept01.htm |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2007-10-07 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080708224524/http://www.d3hoops.com/notable/01/julyaugsept01.htm |archivedate=2008-07-08 }}</ref> He spent the 2002 [[NBA Summer League]] with the [[New York Knicks]], and the 2003 Summer League with the [[Seattle SuperSonics]].<ref name=nytimes/>

Horace Jenkins got his break in the summer of 2004, playing in the NBA Summer League with the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He was previously playing with [[AEK Athens BC|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basket League]], with Pistons draft pick [[Andreas Glyniadakis]]. Pistons President [[Joe Dumars]] was watching film of Glyniadakis, and spotted Jenkins. Jenkins averaged 20.1 points, 3.3 assists, and 1.8 steals in 12 [[EuroLeague]] games with AEK Athens. Impressed, Dumars invited Jenkins to summer camp in 2004. In summer camp, he averaged 8.2 points and 2.8 assists per game in 5 games. That was enough to garner a guaranteed contract from the Pistons, which he signed on August 4, 2004. His contract was a one-year deal worth $385,277.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/transactions_jenkins_040804.html|title = Pistons Sign Guard Horace Jenkins|website = [[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

Jenkins started the [[2004–05 NBA season]] on the injured list, but he did see NBA game action 15 times. He was on the bench for the raising of the Pistons' 2004 championship banner, as well as the [[Pacers–Pistons brawl]]. Rumors circulated that he was being traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]], and also that he was going to leave the Pistons, and return to Italy. His NBA debut was a two-minute stint against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He scored 9 points the next night against the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. Jenkins scored a career-high 10 points on December 10, 2004, against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He was one of only three Pistons to score in double figures in that game. He scored 2 points in his home state of New Jersey against the [[Brooklyn Nets|Nets]] on February 5, 2005. Five nights later, in a rematch of the [[2004 NBA Finals]], Jenkins scored 8 points, in only 6 minutes against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

Jenkins' final NBA game was on April 20, 2005, in a 86–97 loss to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] where he recorded 6 points, 2 rebounds and 1 steal in 20 minutes of playing time (the most minutes he ever played in a game).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/stats/2004/index.html |title=PISTONS: 2004–2005 Pistons Regular Statistics |website=www.nba.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050706111517/http://www.nba.com/pistons/stats/2004/index.html |archive-date=2005-07-06}}</ref>

Although he was left off the playoff roster, the Pistons made the [[NBA Finals]] for the second straight year. Jenkins was notable for being one of the oldest rookies in the NBA, and his life story was the subject of a short presentation narrated by [[Jamie Foxx]], on [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], during the [[2005 NBA Finals]]. Jenkins took the long route to the NBA, working to support his family, and then playing in Europe, before signing his first NBA contract, at the age of 29.

In 2005, Jenkins signed a contract with the [[Israel]]i team [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]], who had gotten sponsored by billionaire [[Arkadi Gaydamak]] shortly before. He quickly became the star of the team (rivaling the former star from 2 years prior, [[Will Solomon]], who played for their arch rivals [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] that season), and led it to the [[ULEB Cup|EuroCup]] semifinals and to the [[Israeli Basketball Super League|Israeli League]] Finals.

In the summer of 2006, he signed with the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish League]] giants [[Efes Pilsen SK|Efes Pilsen]]. In the middle of the 2006–07 season, he returned to Hapoel Jerusalem, after personal problems with his Turkish [[head coach]] arose (after the accusation from the previous year had been dropped), and he helped the team reach the [[Ligat Winner|Israeli league]] [[Final Four]], in which the team lost to arch rivals [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]. On August 3, 2007, Jenkins signed with the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] team [[Fortitudo Bologna|Climamio Bologna]], on a one-year contract.
